title: CGM Time-in-Range by Meal Window
dataSources: Continuous glucose (`cgm:glucose`), HRV (`hrv:reading`), mood check-ins (`mood:checkin`), ketone readings (`ketone:reading`), reaction-time trials (`reaction:trial`), sauna sessions (`sauna:session`), resting temperature (`temp:reading`), and meditation logs (`meditation:session`).
app: Biohacking telemetry from CGMs, HRV devices, ketone meters, mood and meditation journals, reaction-time apps, sauna logs, and health sensors streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=cgm:glucose
| stats avg(time_in_range_pct) as avg_time_in_range_pct by meal_window
| sort meal_window
description: Compares average glucose time-in-range across breakfast, lunch, dinner, and late-evening eating windows.
value: Meal timing often matters as much as meal content, and a by-window view gives you a practical way to learn that pattern.
implementation: Export daily CGM summaries with a meal-window label derived from food logs or scheduled eating periods.
visualization: Bar chart of average time-in-range by meal window.
grandmaExplanation: It watches which times of day are easiest or hardest for keeping your glucose in a healthy range.
